topics.topic_label: Enterprise agent platforms (the most detailed multi-company production write-up in months — Lyft at 270,000 AI Assist interactions/month and 65% deflection, Super TOBi at ~9.5M customers and 82% resolution, LATAM's Concierge on 3–5% margins; Databricks extends free Genie usage six months, which is what you do when agent-product adoption is behind plan)

Multi-agent coordination (Lyft's router meta-agent dispatches to subagents that are themselves complete state graphs and can hand control back mid-conversation; LATAM found every specialist independently structuring output for no downstream consumer — moving it to the supervisor once cut cost ~15% at no quality loss)

Implementation & services revenue (the number that matters in the CX write-up is organisational, not architectural — configurable agents initialised from a JSON config plus a domain expert's prompt took build time from ~6 months to ~2 weeks, after which 'the platform was no longer the primary constraint; prompt and evaluation quality were')

Evaluation gap (execution, outcome and experience named as three different questions an agent can split on — a scheduler that books exactly as instructed but never confirms the timezone; Lyft had to make its simulated customers *worse* because articulate LLM users produced >90% offline pass rates that died in production; LATAM found 95% of 'out of scope' classifications were real needs)

Enterprise agent platforms (all eight mandatory enterprise vendors returned zero dated items — a genuinely quiet day at the platform layer, with the two items that landed coming from outside it: Databricks and OpenAI running 'Agents at Work' across three regions on the Agent Bricks + Unity AI Gateway pattern, and Flowise, a well-known visual flow-builder, announcing it is shutting down)

Multi-agent coordination (four papers in one batch and all four are negative results — multi-agent debate converges on systematically biased consensus, non-English orchestration degrades in ways English-only benchmarks never surface, a small amount of injected misinformation collapses collective fact recovery when evidence is split across agents, and concurrent agents need stateful governance rather than per-call checks)

Implementation & services revenue (the labour side of the trade shows up in the Swiss job file — the forward-deployed-engineer title has spanned Team Lead to zero-years-required inside one country in one week, and the newest posting names no LLM, RAG, prompt or agent requirement at all, listing Claude and Gemini in the benefits stack beside Kubernetes and Postgres)

Evaluation gap (frontier science benchmarks are being passed by shortcut rather than reasoning, so headline scores overstate capability — which lands the same day as this week's automated-mathematics claims and a benchmark-saturation study on the HN front page; the eval-practice answer is that the bottleneck has moved from writing evals to stopping agents from grading their own homework)

Multi-agent coordination (a rare post-mortem reports what got deleted rather than what got built - agent-flow and orchestrated hand-off survived, free-form peer collaboration only in bounded, heavily instrumented niches; ASGE-RR supplies the scheduling primitive MCP and A2A specify a wire format for but leave undefined, and a supply-chain narrative names agent-to-agent validation, not agent quality, as the bottleneck)

Implementation & services revenue (the last-mile thesis gets a matching JD - Orange Business puts 'advising C-level stakeholders on AI strategy, governance, and roadmaps' inside an engineering role, which is the same claim a French practitioner tribune makes from the other side: raw model capability has become a commodity and the contest is decided after the demo; SAP's proof point is a customer cutting HR cycle times 40-60%)

The evaluation gap (benchmark trust cracked in public - a commenter screenshotted the Artificial Analysis agentic index flipping both order and scores between two page loads minutes apart, and Meta was caught comparing against a mid-tier rival model and still losing rows to it; on the same day EuroExec shows frontier models fall short of expert judgment on European executive tasks, DelusionEval instruments a failure mode that has driven product-safety headlines all year, and AV-AIVAT cuts agent-eval cost ~74x with certified anytime-valid stopping)

Multi-agent coordination (emergent inter-agent coordination is now an incident-report fact rather than a thought experiment — a stuck OpenAI agent left a note in a shared writable Artifactory store asking other agents for a file, more agents found the improvised message board and used it; on the product side A2A is framed as the handoff layer between role-specific agents that share one centralised MCP server, and stablyai/orca holds at +648 while its fleet-orchestration peer multica cools to +173)

Evaluation gap (the sharpest item of the day is a reproducibility challenge — a commenter screenshots the Artificial Analysis agentic leaderboard flipping both order AND scores between two page loads minutes apart with identical chart copy, Qwen 55.4 vs Opus Max 55.3 then Opus Max 59.2 vs Qwen 58.4; IBM's Benchmarking the Benchmarks meta-evaluates which conversational-agent benchmarks actually discriminate, and the recurring caveat on DeepSeek V4-Flash is benchmark-versus-long-horizon divergence)
